whatHappens.text: The city dresses for the night: a tailor locks up, a teenager practises a dance step at a bus stop, a grandmother hangs a jewel-green dress on a fire escape to air. On a balcony, a woman dances alone in her kitchen. Across the street, a neighbour lifts a phone toward her. The lens glows copper: the Ember, the city's everyday "no." The neighbour lowers it, embarrassed. She raises a glass to him and keeps dancing. No dialogue, music only.

whatHappens.text: - Thursday night becomes Friday. At 2 a.m., when every club in the city has just closed, the Riverside Pavilion opens: a Private Exchange in the old tradition of the breakfast dance, a party that begins when the others end. - A room of evening clothes at the wrong hour. The band swings until four, then the kitchen sends out chicken and waffles, grits and salmon croquettes on silver. Night nurses arrive off shift in scrubs and earrings. Dee's 1985 relay teammates wear their old warm-up jackets over sequins. Zuri's teammates came for the food and stay for the band. Sloane hosts in a gown and carries her sneakers. - At 5:40 the band stops mid-song and the whole party walks out to the bleachers, shoes in hand. Honora Vance is already there in a camel coat with a thermos; she came for the race, not the party. Sloane sits two rows behind her and doesn't push it. - Before the start, lane four lights up: the Echo Track, a pale line of light that runs Dee's 1985 record stride for stride, drawn from the city's archive footage of her own race. Zuri looks at it, then at Dee: "That's you?" "That was me." - The gun is Gideon clapping once. Dee's start is everything the footage promised: she leads for forty metres. Then Zuri goes past her, and past the line of light too. The bleachers, in last night's clothes, lose their minds. - Dee finishes bent double, laughing so hard she can't stand up. That was the request all along: to be beaten by someone worth it, with her best self running beside her. Zuri, catching her breath: "Next Friday."
